subject: Oceanography
title: Whale Falls
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Whale Falls.

hook.text: When a whale dies and sinks, its body feeds an entire ecosystem on the seafloor—for up to 100 years.

buildup.text: First, scavengers like hagfish and sleeper sharks consume the soft tissue—this takes months to years.

discovery.text: Then enrichment opportunists colonize the bones—worms and crustaceans living off the remaining organic matter.

twist.text: Finally, sulfophilic bacteria break down bone lipids—creating a mini vent-like ecosystem for decades.

climax.text: Whale falls may serve as stepping stones—connecting isolated vent and seep communities across the deep.

punchline.text: A dead whale gives the deepest ocean a century of life.

quiz.question: How long can a whale fall support a deep-sea ecosystem?
